title: Headless G1 precision: P0 commands judged by truth on the headless side only
description:
Found by the independent verification of murmur-8ak's fix round 1 (2026-10-10). Not fixed: filed for a later round.

CRITERIA.md's precision (eval/headless/CRITERIA.md, as amended 2026-10-10) judges a human-tier P0 command (`safety.low_reserve`, `safety.stuck`) by whether its fault was real by truth: the vehicle's true charge, or a scripted stop. Only headless records carry the truth of our vehicles (`truth.ours`, the stand-ins' own state every 2 s); a full-stack record has none, so `metrics.p0_fault_real` returns None there and the proposal is listed as unjudged and left out of the proportion. The two sides therefore judge P0 commands differently.

No effect on G1 so far: in Harbor watch the P0 commands are auto-tier under the shipped watch policy, so none enters precision on either side. It would matter for any situation where a P0 command waits for a person.

Possible fix: record our vehicles' truth on the full stack (the stand-in engine's state, or the bridge's own reported battery as a stated proxy) and judge both sides alike, or keep P0 out of the gated precision on both sides; either needs a dated CRITERIA.md section.

title: Headless simulator: stand-in and bridge phases fixed across episodes; the playbook's first tick drawn wider than the full stack's
description:
Found by the independent verification of murmur-8ak's fix round 1 (2026-10-10). Not fixed: filed for a later round.

The headless simulator's process phases are the same in every episode, where the full stack's vary run to run:

- Battery report ages at the opening orders' checks are identical in every headless seed (0.90, 0.28 and 0.84 s for the three vehicles reported), against 0.3 to 1.3 s across the full-stack runs (reviewer's scratchpad/rev-headless/battery_age.py over logs/headless-g1/gate2 and gate2-headless in the murmur-8ak worktree). The stand-ins' start (`standins_start_s`, a median) and their stream phases are fixed; only the emulator's draws and the stand-ins' own draws vary.
- The playbook's first tick after `ai_start_s` is drawn uniformly over 0.711 to 1.590 s (the six calibration runs' range, seeds 101 to 106), while 19 of the 20 gate runs (seeds 1 to 20) came at 1.28 to 1.41 s (0.46 and 0.52 s in the other two). Gate seeds may not be fitted on: narrowing the range needs more calibration seeds (107 and up, CRITERIA.md's rule), then a dated CRITERIA.md section before any gate re-run.

Where it can matter: a check or a preview at a fact-age boundary (seed 18 of the G1 re-run: a 10.6 s battery report against the 10 s limit decided a proposal), and the phase of every playbook tick against the bridge's 1 s loops.

Possible fix: draw the stand-ins' start and the first tick per episode seed from distributions measured on more calibration runs.

title: After a crash, lost-link values carried from the earlier run's log hold no queued mission

Also from the same review: .last-run is rewritten even when the carry failed (crates/murmur-bridge/src/decision/engage.rs ~756), so an earlier log's debt drops out of the chain with only an inbox alert; keep pointing at the log still owed until its debt is carried or explicitly written off by an operator. And a bridge crash mid carry_from loop (engage.rs ~765-790) leaves a partial carried set, which replay's 'every owed platform carried' would reject: make the carry atomic or log it as one event.

title: A queued newer order abandons an engagement's intercept as a system stop and flies the fallback
description: Final review of rules 6 (present on master 5444976, not from the merge). A newer order queued for an engagement's platform makes supersede_queued abandon the engagement's unstarted intercept (crates/murmur-bridge/src/decision/queue.rs around 239); the engagement loop reads that as an intercept failure (engage.rs around 970), stops with cause 'system: the platform's intercept failed: abandoned ... The stop cause is mislabeled for evaluation (Phase G counts causes) and the operator's order is contradicted until it leaves the queue. Fix: treat a queued newer order like a dispatched one (superseded, no fallback), or decide explicitly and record it in DECISIONS.md.

title: Headless runner: no cancel of an opening order a scripted id approved at submission (the live runner cancels it)
description:
Found in murmur-8ak's review (fix round 1, unaddressed edge case; filed 2026-10-10). Not fixed.

The live situation runner (eval/situation_run.py `issue_order`) checks each opening order op-setup submits: if the answer shows it approved at submission by a scripted id (`self_authorized`: a fact changed between the dry run and the submission), it cancels the intent unless it went out already (`undo_self_authorized`, `POST /api/intents/{id}/cancel`) and records a loud problem. The headless runner (eval/headless/episode.py `Runner.issue_orders`) submits the same way after the same dry run but never makes that check or cancel.

No effect in Harbor watch or the families so far: the dry run and the submission happen at one simulated instant, so the facts cannot change between them and the case cannot arise headless as built. It would if the runner ever waited between the two. Fix: port `self_authorized` and `undo_self_authorized` into `Runner.issue_orders` (record `self_authorized` in the order's record as live does) and test it with a stubbed answer.

title: Headless session adapter: a protocol error raises RuntimeError, the live session McpError
description:
Found in murmur-8ak's review (fix round 1, unaddressed edge case; filed 2026-10-10). Not fixed.

On an MCP protocol error (an unknown tool, invalid parameters), the live session (agents/policy_agent.py `AgentSession.call` through agents/scripted_agent.py `call`, the MCP SDK's `ClientSession.call_tool`) raises the SDK's `McpError`; the headless session adapter (eval/headless/sim.py `HeadlessSession._call`) raises `RuntimeError(<protocol error message>)`. A tool-level error (`isError`) raises `RuntimeError("<tool>: <error>")` on both sides, as it should.

No effect today: the playbook's engine catches `Exception` around every session call. A client that catches `McpError` specifically would behave differently headless. Fix: raise `mcp.shared.exceptions.McpError` with the same `ErrorData` (code and message) the SDK would build, and add the case to eval/headless/tests/test_session.py.

title: Headless simulator: run.started and the first anchor stamped at t = 0, about 1.02 s before live
description:
Found by the independent verification of murmur-8ak's fix round 1 (2026-10-10). Not fixed: filed for a later round.

In the headless simulator, the bridge's `run.started` audit event and its first anchor (`why: start`) are stamped at t = 0 (the simulator builds the decision layer with `Decision::load` at the episode's start), while on the full stack the decision layer starts about 1.02 s after the situation's zero (first anchor 1.016 to 1.048 s over calibration runs 101 to 106 and the gate runs). Fix round 1 made the bridge's loops start, and its sockets answer, at `bridge_start_s` (1.024 s), but `Decision::load` still runs at 0, so its start stamp and the anchors' first entry are about 1 s early against live.

Effect seen: none on the playbook's proposals or the G1 metrics (nothing reads the start stamp); audit logs compared across the two sides differ there. Fix: build the decision layer at `bridge_start_s` (crates/murmur-headless/src/sim/mod.rs `assemble`), keeping the order main.rs uses.
